SN-TS2Vec change point model

Source: R/cpd_members.R
ts2vec.Rd

Trains the unsupervised SN-TS2Vec model of Bazarova et al. (2024), as used in the WWAggr code: the TS2Vec encoder of Yue et al. (2022) (a linear input layer and residual blocks of dilated convolutions with GELU) with spectral normalisation of the convolutions, trained with the hierarchical contrastive loss of TS2Vec on two overlapping random crops of every sequence. The change score of a step is 1 minus the cosine similarity of the max-pooled embeddings of the two consecutive windows that end at it (see cpd_scores()).

Usage

ts2vec(
  x,
  window = 4,
  output_dim = 32,
  hidden_dim = 128,
  depth = 8,
  spectral_norm = TRUE,
  mask = c("binomial", "continuous", "all_true"),
  temporal_unit = 0,
  max_train_length = NULL,
  learning_rate = 0.001,
  weight_decay = 0.2,
  batch_size = 128,
  epochs = 40,
  patience = 40,
  validation = NULL,
  step = 1,
  alpha = 1,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Training sequences, in the formats accepted by indid().

window

Length of the history and future windows of the scores.

output_dim, hidden_dim

Sizes of the embedding and of the hidden channels.

depth

Number of hidden residual blocks (one more maps to output_dim).

spectral_norm

Whether the convolutions are spectrally normalised (largest singular value at most 1).

mask

Masking of the input during training: "binomial" (each step kept with probability 0.5), "continuous" (5 masked segments of 10 % of the length) or "all_true" (no masking).

temporal_unit

Smallest level of the hierarchy with a temporal loss.

max_train_length

If set, longer training sequences are cut at a random offset to this length.

learning_rate, weight_decay

Settings of AdamW; the learning rate follows a cosine schedule with warm restarts (periods of 10 epochs, then 1000).

batch_size

Number of sequences per batch.

epochs

Largest number of epochs.

patience

Early stopping on the validation loss (only with validation data).

validation

Optional validation sequences.

step, alpha

Prediction settings, as in tscp2().

seed

Seed of the private random stream (weights, crops, masks, dropout, order of the batches). NULL draws one from the session.

Value

A ts2vec object with the parameters, the power iteration vectors, the settings and the losses of every epoch.

Details

The model follows the reference code (https://github.com/stalex2902/wwagr-ensemble-cpd, src/baselines/ts2vec_sn.py and prediction_utils.py):

  • Spectral normalisation divides a weight by its largest singular value when it exceeds 1. The singular value is estimated by one power iteration at every forward pass in training (15 at initialisation), as torch.nn.utils.parametrizations.spectral_norm.

  • Training masks the hidden representation of the input steps, and applies dropout (0.1) to the output.

  • The window embedding is the maximum over its steps.

The network, its gradients and AdamW are written in R. The defaults are those of the Human Activity configuration of the reference (configs/human_activity_ts2vec.yaml).

References

Bazarova, A., Romanenkova, E. and Zaytsev, A. (2024). Normalizing self-supervised learning for provably reliable change point detection. 2024 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM), 21-30.

Yue, Z., Wang, Y., Duan, J., Yang, T., Huang, C., Tong, Y. and Xu, B. (2022). TS2Vec: Towards universal representation of time series. Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 36(8), 8980-8987.

Stepikin, A., Romanenkova, E. and Zaytsev, A. (2025). WWAggr: A window Wasserstein-based aggregation for ensemble change point detection. 2025 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM), 1535-1544. doi:10.1109/ICDM65498.2025.00163

See also

cpd_scores(), cpd_ensemble(), dfr_wwaggr().

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- array(stats::rnorm(8 * 12 * 2), c(8, 12, 2))
model <- ts2vec(x, window = 3, output_dim = 4, hidden_dim = 6, depth = 2, epochs = 2, seed = 1)
model
#> SN-TS2Vec model: windows of 3 steps, 2 feature(s), embedding of size 4, 2 epoch(s)
